thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall — high error spike observed for /v1/chat/generate and elevated tail latency across chat routes. Alert: 5xx_rate > 15% (3m window) and p95 latency > 1.5s. Investigate immediately. Links: https://observability.local/alerts/INC-2026-231  
Alice Nguyen: I'm on it, joining. pulling traces now.  
Ben Parker: grabbing logs + rate metrics. My first suspicion is a bursty producer or caching pressure on KV caches.  
Samantha Li: I can look at runtime logs and model hosts, if it's KV cache thrash we may see increased model rewarm.  
Maya Patel: Support FYI — customers may see retries on chat and some embedding requests delayed. I've started a search for incoming tickets.  
Alice Nguyen: Quick check — dashboards show chat traffic has a sustained 3x increase from region-us-west-2 starting ~1916500600. embeddings and rerank are flat.  
Ben Parker: Confirmed. Chat engine pool CPU stayed steady but queue depth on the chat routing layer jumped.  
Samantha Li: Copy. I'm SSHing into runtime nodes. If routing layer is overwhelmed we can apply route-specific limits at the edge to protect embeddings.  
Carlos Mendez: Product wants minimal customer-visible change. Can we deprioritize public chat traffic and keep embeddings/rerank for enterprise customers?  
Alice Nguyen: Plan suggestion: 1) Apply temporary per-endpoint rate limits: reduce /v1/chat/* to 40rpm/org (from 120rpm), 2) Keep embeddings at current quota, 3) Disable rerank batch endpoint for public tier (serve enterprise only) — this protects cost and latency for embeddings.  
Ibrahim Khan: Agree. Also enable circuit-breaker fallback to smaller chat model for best-effort requests.  
Ben Parker: Ready to push a soft limit at the gateway — rate limiting rule + route tag. I'll apply a short-lived rule that is easy to rollback.  
Alice Nguyen: Runbook step: post mitigation commands and keep paste of what we ran.  
Ben Parker: Executing now.  
Ben Parker: /gatewayctl apply -f -  ```yaml
# temporary route limits applied during incident
rules:
  - name: chat-temp-throttle
    route: /v1/chat/*
    scope: public
    limit: 40rpm
    action: 429
  - name: rerank-disable-public
    route: /v1/rerank/*
    scope: public
    action: reject
```  
incident-bot: Deploy started by ben.p at 1916501298. CI job: ci/gateway/rate-limits/231  
Samantha Li: I see the gateway rule pushed and propagated to edge nodes. Applying model fallback policy on runtime:  
Samantha Li: ```sh
# enable fallback to "chat-medium" for non-enterprise orgs
rwi runtime apply-policy --policy=chat_fallback_med --scope=public --ttl=30m
```  
Maya Patel: Noted, telling support to mark potential degraded chat UX but embeddings and enterprise rerank unaffected.  
Carlos Mendez: Can we whitelist a few enterprise orgs for chat full quota? We should keep high-value customers unharmed.  
Alice Nguyen: Yes — adding org allowlist for chat. Ben, can you add exemptions for the 6 enterprise org IDs?  
Ben Parker: Added allowlist: orgs [ent-1234, ent-5678, ent-9012, ent-3344, ent-7788, ent-4455] — those bypass the 40rpm throttle. Confirmed on edge.  
Ibrahim Khan: Runtime metrics: p95 for chat dropped from 1.6s to 0.9s within 45s of applying throttle. Error rate down to 4% after 3 min.  
Alice Nguyen: Good. Can we keep rerank disabled for public until traffic cools?  
Samantha Li: Rerank public route is now returning 403 for new requests. Enterprise rerank still routed to dedicated pool.  
Maya Patel: Logged customer-visible status: "Degraded chat performance for public apps; embeddings and enterprise features unaffected. Working on mitigations." Posting to status.redwood.ai/incidents/1916501234  
Carlos Mendez: Do we have an estimate for restoration?  
Alice Nguyen: We'll monitor for 15 more minutes; if rate and latency remain stable we'll gradually relax throttle to 80rpm then to 120rpm. ETA tentative 30-60m.  
Ben Parker: Pasting commands used for rollback (keep in runbook):  
Ben Parker: ```sh
# rollback throttle
/gatewayctl delete rule chat-temp-throttle
/gatewayctl delete rule rerank-disable-public
# remove allowlist (if needed)
/gatewayctl update allowlist --remove ent-4455,ent-7788
```  
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-231, severity: S2. Link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-231  
Ibrahim Khan: Quick customer impact assessment: ~2.3% of active orgs hit the throttle in the first 10m; of those ~0.4% are enterprise (all whitelisted). We should expect uptick in 429s for public apps.  
Maya Patel: Support update: ticket surge small but rising, sending templated reply to affected customers, offering priority retry guidance.  
Alice Nguyen: Monitoring windows: watch p95, 5xx_rate, queue_depth, and KV cache miss rate. Any sign of cache thrash we'll revert fallback.  
Samantha Li: Observability note — root cause still unknown; correlating upstream producer logs. Could be a misconfigured integration doing fan-out.  
Ben Parker: I'll also add short-lived quota changes in billing for public tier to avoid overbilling refunds if customers retry: temporarily extend grace (no extra charge) while we stabilize.  
Carlos Mendez: Approving grace extension for the incident window.  
Alice Nguyen: Handoff: @oncall (today) to @oncall (tomorrow) at 1916505600 — I'll leave mitigation sticky until handoff. Next steps: 1) keep throttle, 2) stabilize metrics for 15m, 3) schedule post-incident blameless RCA.  
Ibrahim Khan: I'll capture traces and top talkers list and dump into the incident doc.  
Maya Patel: Support will prepare customer outreach draft for postmortem.  
Alice Nguyen: Thanks team — keeping thread open. If anything spikes we escalate to S1.  
Ben Parker: Metrics look stable at 1916502000, p95 ~0.85s, 5xx 3.8%. I'll mark mitigation as active.  
incident-bot: Reminder: please attach any runbook edits to INC-2026-231 and update status page when closing.  
Alice Nguyen: Closing note for shift handoff: leave throttle in place until next oncall validates ramp down.  
Ibrahim Khan: Uploaded top-talkers CSV to incident doc.  
Maya Patel: Draft customer post: "We experienced a temporary spike in chat traffic affecting response times for public apps. We throttled public chat to protect overall system availability; enterprise and embeddings were not affected. We will follow up with a root cause and remediation plan."  
Alice Nguyen: End of thread for now.
